crossRefs.note: “Through the window she looked out, and cried: Sisera’s mother looked through the lattice. ‘Why is his chariot so long…
For at the window of my house, I looked out through my lattice.
My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances…
Let your spring be blessed. Rejoice in the wife of your youth.
A loving doe and a graceful deer— let her breasts satisfy you at all times. Be captivated always with her love.
Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your life of vanity, which he has given you under the sun…
For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons will marry you. As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God…

people.name: Abimelech
people.line: Philistine king who interacted with Abraham and Isaac

people.name: Isaac
people.line: Son of Abraham; father of Jacob and Esau.

people.name: Philistia
people.line: An ancient people and region in Canaan

people.name: Rebekah
people.line: Wife of Isaac; mother of Jacob and Esau

translations.web: When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was caressing Rebekah, his wife.
translations.bsb: When Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down from the window and was surprised to see Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.
translations.kjv: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.
translations.asv: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.
